answers.core: This is a very common animation functionality in games (to the point where a lot of RPGs only have 3-frame 'bounce' animations in their spritesheets)
answers.workaround: In theory you can unwrap bounce animations into loop animations by basically doubling the amount of frames you use on your tilesheet, but that's more work, creates a bunch of duplicate tiles, and means that godot's animation system isn't compatible with existing tilesets that assume you can bounce your animations.

title: Tilemap: Add 'bounce' or 'Ping-Pong' animation order to animated tiles
